sections.body:
This is a story about a tiny seed. The seed is so small that you could lose it on your hand. It is smaller than a pea.

A good story has a shape. It has a beginning, a middle, and an end. The beginning tells you who the characters are. The middle brings a problem. The end fixes the problem in a way you did not expect.

This story has that shape. In the beginning, the seed is buried in dark soil. In the middle, the seed waits for rain and sun. In the end, the seed becomes a tree.

The story is quiet, and that is part of its magic. Read it slowly. Let the words arrive at the same speed as the growing.

Listen first. Then tell the story back to someone. That is how a story becomes yours.
examples: This story has a beginning, a middle and an end.
The seed is smaller than a pea.
I can tell this story again tomorrow.
sections.heading: What this story is about

sections.body:
A small brown seed falls from the pod of a maple tree. It lands in the soft soil under the grass.

The seed does not see the sun. It does not feel the wind. Above it, the grass is bright and green.

The seed waits. This is hard work. Waiting is the hardest thing a seed can do.

Winter comes. The soil is cold. Then spring comes, and the soil is warm again.

Then the rain comes. It falls through the grass and soaks into the ground. The seed drinks. The seed swells.

Something starts to push. It is a root. The root grows down, into the dark, looking for water.
examples: The seed landed in the soft soil.
The seed waited through the cold winter.
The rain came, and the seed drank.
sections.heading: The beginning: a dark place under the grass

sections.body:
Down in the dark, the root grows. It is thin and pale, and it is very strong.

The seed is a problem now. It sits in the middle of the soil with a root below it. It cannot go back up. It cannot go down. It is stuck.

Then the sun comes down through the grass. It is warm. It tells the seed to grow upward, toward the light.

So the seed pushes. It pushes past the stones. It pushes past a beetle's house. It pushes and pushes until one dark morning, something green appears above the soil.

It is a tiny green shoot. It is so little. It leans towards the sun, because that is where the sun is.
examples: The root grew down into the dark.
The seed could not go back up or down.
The tiny green shoot leaned towards the sun.
sections.heading: The middle: a push and a pull

sections.body:
The little shoot grows. Its leaves come out. It grows taller than your knee. It grows taller than your head.

Then summer comes, and the tree grows wider. The branches reach out like open arms.

Years pass. One spring, the tree is covered in flowers. Pink and white flowers, all the way up.

And then the birds come. They find the branches and the warm leaves. They build nests. They sing all day.

The seed that was smaller than a pea is now a tree where a hundred birds live.

The ground where the seed slept is still the same small patch of soil. But look up. Look up.
examples: The branches reached out like open arms.
The tree was covered in flowers.
Look up, and you see a hundred birds.
sections.heading: The surprise: a tree full of birds

sections.body:
These are the words you will meet in this story. Learn them here, and you can use them in your own sentences.

A **seed** is the small beginning of a plant. Inside a seed is everything the plant needs to start.

A **root** is the part that grows down into the soil. Roots hold the plant up and drink up the water.

A **sprout** is a baby plant that has just come out of the soil. It is very small and very green.

Soil is the soft earth where plants grow. It holds water and food for the roots.

Sunlight is the light from the sun. Plants lean towards it, because they need it to grow.
examples: A seed is the beginning of a plant.
The root grows down and the shoot grows up.
The sprout leaned towards the sun.
sections.heading: The words inside this story

terms.example: The seed was smaller than a pea.
terms.gloss: The small beginning of a plant. It holds everything the plant needs to start.

terms.example: The root drank the rain deep in the ground.
terms.gloss: The part of a plant that grows down into the soil, to hold it up and drink water.

terms.example: A green sprout appeared above the soil.
terms.gloss: A baby plant that has just come out of the soil. Very small, very green.

terms.example: The seed fell into the soft brown soil.
terms.gloss: The soft earth where plants grow. It holds water and food for the roots.

terms.example: The leaves turned towards the sunlight.
terms.gloss: The light from the sun. Plants need it and lean towards it.

sections.body:
What did the seed learn? The seed learned that small things are not wasted. A seed the size of a pea can hold a whole tree inside it, and it needs time, rain, and sun.

That is a good thing to remember. When you feel small and not ready, keep going. You are still growing.

Here is how to tell this story to someone. Keep the order, and the surprise will land in the right place.

Start with who the story is about. Tell the problem in the middle. Save the surprise for last. Then say the small lesson in one short sentence.

The lesson of this story is this: little things grow big with time and care.
examples: The story starts with a tiny seed.
The surprise comes at the end.
Little things grow big with time and care.
sections.heading: The small lesson, and how to tell the story
steps: Start by naming the character: a tiny seed under the grass.
Tell the problem: the seed is stuck in the dark soil.
Tell the middle: rain wakes it, and the sun pulls it up.
End with the surprise and the lesson: a tree full of birds.

item.summary: A small seed falls into the dark soil and waits. Follow it through the rain, the sun and the seasons until it becomes a tree with birds in its branches. After reading, you can retell the story, use its new words, and explain its lesson about patience and care.
item.title: A Tiny Seed's Big Adventure
